entries.test: Representative outputs from the Sora version discussed, together with public technical documentation and controlled evaluations, would establish whether object disappearances routinely occur and reflect pixel prediction rather than physical-state computation.
entries.note: The claim includes both observable failures and an assertion about their mechanism; videos alone would establish only the former.

entries.test: Public architectural evidence and controlled tests that pit visual-sequence regularities against physical constraints would test whether Sora represents objects and whether image prediction invariably overrides physics.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supports the causal connection expressed in the normalization. “Whenever” and “only” make this an absolute claim.

entries.test: Public technical documentation and evaluations would establish whether Sora's frame prediction approximates appearances without computing physical states and their evolution under physical laws.
entries.note: The preceding physics-engine discussion supplies a concrete reading of “physics.” “Fine” is evaluative, but the central distinction is a factual assertion about the modeling method.
